mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 3.25% in the month prior to the prediction date leads to a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 3.25% in the month preceding the prediction date
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the mean of the preceding 60 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in hourly wage growth (implied via UNRATE falling) signals weak labor market momentum, which is associated with negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a month while UNRATE falls by >0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: In 20 consecutive such labor weakening events, the 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% for three consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as it reflects robust economic momentum and investor optimism.
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, the 60-day forward returns do not outperform the mean of the previous 12 months (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3% for two consecutive months indicates deflationary pressure, which tends to compress equity valuations and drive negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: During 5 such deflationary months, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the prior 5-month average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.5% for the first time in three months while the Fed Funds rate remains below 2%, it signals a shift toward accommodative policy, which is associated with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.5% and FEDFUNDS < 2% for three consecutive months, then UNRATE falls below 4.5% in the fourth month
regime_hint: Policy divergence: low unemployment & low rates
failure_condition: Across 10 such policy divergence episodes, the 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly surge in both retail sales (implied via HOUST) and manufacturing activity (GDPC1) above their 12-month moving averages suggests resilient demand, which predicts a positive S&P 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: In 8 such dual-demand acceleration events, the 20-day forward returns do not exceed the mean of the prior 8 windows (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in labor force participation (PAYEMS) without a corresponding rise in unemployment suggests demographic headwinds, which is associated with negative S&P 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 15 such participation declines, the 5-day forward returns are not persistently negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in consumer prices (CPIAUCSL) followed within the same month by a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates supply-side weakness and is associated with a negative S&P 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls by >1.5% in a month and INDPRO falls by >3% in the same month
failure_condition: During 4 such supply shocks, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline (p > 0.05).
